_comment: Boolean-fact demo policy: proves the companion's fact-checking generalizes beyond numeric prices to a yes/no fact (live chat availability). Uses the built-in categories (no "categories" key). Point the fact's source_url at demo-page/availability.html served locally: go run ./cmd/demoserver -dir demo-page -addr 127.0.0.1:8001, then run the companion with -provider direct -policy examples/policy.boolean-demo.json -evidence-ttl 5s. Edit demo-page/availability.html's 'available'/'unavailable' word to flip the demo.

facts._comment: source_pattern and answer_pattern are intentionally the same regex: they both just capture the whole 'live chat ...' clause, however it is worded, up to the end of the sentence. The compare=boolean logic (internal/extract) then reduces whatever was captured to true/false by scanning it for a small set of yes/no signal words (available, unavailable, online, offline, not available, ...), rather than requiring an exact wording match the way the numeric/exact comparators do.
facts.name: Live chat availability
